title: The New Orleans drummer feel and passing it on
summary: The shared New Orleans feel is hard to describe; advice to young drummers to avoid attitude and help others.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What is that commonality that New Orleans drummers have? That separates from? I don't know.
It's hard. You walk in Chicago.

What's that? It's a certain, well you can't write it, you know. It's hard to describe. It's more of a feeling I would think. You know, because you can hear something and you say, hey that's a New Orleans piece. It's just like the second line, I don't want to wear that out, but you know when you hear a second line piece. A lot of times, Idris could be playing and I say, Idris, that's a New Orleans drummer. I hear something by James Black with someone else, Smokey, you know, Blackwell. And I say that's a New Orleans drummer. You know, I'm not saying like a tenor saxophone, they know the sound of another horn, but it's just something about, maybe you have to be a drummer. You know, another one that sounds ridiculous, but like I said, I hear different things. And I said, I know that's from my own boy, could be one of the younger dudes that's playing, because there's so many young drummers now that's really playing their butt off, you know. Yeah. And I mean I preach a lot of them that don't know me. I don't know them. But I just hope they don't get an attitude, you know, because the beat goes on. But as long as there's New Orleans, there will be drummers. You know, but whatever they have, I hope they can try to pass it on, excuse me, to some of the youngsters. And the youngsters don't grab it and say, hey, this is my original thing, I'm playing it. And nobody else played it, this but me, because what you're playing, somebody else can play it. You just add it a little bit more to it.

You know. Because these guys, like I said, that was just playing the role. Maybe they couldn't swing, but they can play a role. And if you're playing the role today, you play that role when somebody was playing back and blah, blah, blah. Yeah, right. Just keep that, no attitudes is what I'm trying to say. Just learn to play your instrument, do the best that you can, and if you can help somebody with it, help somebody come to you and say, how do you do this?
